board.title: Newsletter · A · The monthly letter
board.name: Newsletter-A · The monthly letter
board.idea: The newsletter is a letter from LCA to its members, and the page where it is made is that letter, open on the screen. One writing column the width of the email, the president's note first, then five short sections under plain headings. What the leaders type is exactly what arrives: mostly words, one photo at most.
board.differs: The least design and the most voice of the four. Anyone who can write an email can make the whole issue in one sitting, there is nothing to arrange, and it reads well in every mail app. It gives up pictures, layout and anything that fills itself in, so an issue is only as good as what someone writes that month.

drawn.title: Newsletter · A · The monthly letter
drawn.second_title: Newsletter · A · The monthly letter, as it arrives
drawn.note:
What: The newsletter is a letter from LCA to its members, and the page where it is made is that letter, open on the screen. Frame A shows one white sheet at the email's own width and type: the subject and inbox preview line, then "Dear members,", the president's note and five plain sections. What the leaders type is exactly what arrives. A Draft status, the send rule and "Mark as ready to send" sit in the rail. Frame B shows the three states, the November report, Settings and a section's History. Part 2 shows the December issue in an inbox, opened on a computer, on two phones (one in the dark setting), and the one-click unsubscribe page. The trade-off: it has the least design and the most voice of the four options, and an issue is only as good as what someone writes that month.

Built from: Nav-Header-Final (the signed-in header), Work-J (the admin chrome, cards and status words; the admin sidebar folds behind "Admin sections" while writing), Work-H-2 (an email written in the workspace), News-Final (the club colour dots and the issue's facts), Tourn-List-Final (the title strip and the December Meet), Home-Final-Phones (the phone bezels) and the kit.

K's feedback applied: LCA admins, the president and the media manager write it together on the site, one person in a section at a time, with History and Restore. It goes out on the same date and time each month unless someone changes this month's. It goes to every member email the site holds, and new members are added when they join. Leaving the newsletter stops this list only. No postal address in any email, as K decided. Open for K: (1) the send rule: someone must mark the issue ready, a reminder goes out the day before, and otherwise nothing is sent; (2) turn-taking or everyone typing at once; (3) the 1st of each month at 8:00 AM Central; (4) each issue readable on the site; (5) whether the newsletter replaces the weekly "News by email" or both run; (6) opens and clicks are not tracked.
unresolved: The letter is drawn in Source Serif 4, loaded from Google Fonts, so the canvas looks the same in every browser. A real email would use Georgia, which every mail app has. Georgia is a little wider, so lines would break slightly differently.

The Work-J admin sidebar is folded behind an 'Admin sections' button on this page. With the 200px outline, the 640px sheet and the 360px rail, there is no room for the sidebar at 1440. This departs from the decided chrome, and the frame label says so.

The third item is the Grand Prix Final, Sat, May 8, 2027, linked to 'Season dates' with no Register, because Tourn-List-Final does not say when its registration opens.

These details are my own and covered by the Sample data badges: the club detail 'next Mon, Dec 7, 2026' (the first Monday after Dec 1, at IHOP per News-Final), 'one Saturday a month' for the youth season, the edit times and the photo description.

board.title: Newsletter · B · The issue, with a cover
board.name: Newsletter-B · The issue, with a cover
board.idea: Every month is an issue with a cover. The leaders build it from numbered pieces: a cover with the month set large, one photo and three cover lines, then a feature and shorter pieces. The page is a builder, with the list of pieces on the left, the piece being written in the middle and the email itself on the right, updating as they type.
board.differs: The most visual of the four, and the one that feels most like a publication people keep. It asks the most of the leaders: one good photo and three cover lines every month, and a little arranging. A navy cover with the rook mark stands in when there is no photo.

board.title: Newsletter · C · The month, built from the site

board.idea: The issue builds itself from what the site already holds, and the leaders only add their words on top. board.title: Newsletter · D · The bulletin, with chess in it
board.name: Newsletter-D · The bulletin, with chess in it
board.idea: A front page with a masthead, and chess on it. The leaders fill the places on a front page: a lead story, Dates to know, shorter pieces, and two things the other options do not have, a Position of the month to solve and a short item of Louisiana chess history. The page where it is made is the front page itself: click a place on it and write. The first position is Paul Morphy's, a New Orleans player, from Paris in 1858.
board.differs: The only option that gives members a reason to open it beyond news: something to solve and something to learn every month. It has the strongest identity of the four and the most to prepare, because someone has to choose a position and a history item each month (a year of them can be prepared ahead and queued).

drawn.note:
What: The newsletter as a front page with a masthead ("Louisiana Chess Bulletin", Vol. 1 · No. 2). It has a lead story, Dates to know, shorter pieces, a Position of the month to solve (Morphy at the opera, Paris, 1858) and an item of Louisiana chess history. It is made on that front page: click a place and write it in the side panel. The left list shows how far each place has got. Of the four options, it has the strongest identity and asks the most preparation. A queue of positions and archive items, prepared months ahead, spreads that work out. Part 2 shows the December issue as a member gets it: on a computer, on a phone, on a phone in dark mode, and the unsubscribe page.

Built from: Nav-Header-Final (signed-in header), Work-J (admin chrome, cards, status words), Work-H-2 (a composer in the kit), News-Final (date tiles, club colour dots, the issue's facts), Tourn-List-Final (title strip, December Meet), Scan-H (the board), Home-Final-Phones (phone bezels).

K's feedback applied: LCA admins, the president and the media manager write it together on the site, one person in a place at a time, with history. It goes out on the same date and time unless changed. It goes to every member email, and new members are added. Unsubscribing stops this list only. No postal address in any email, as K decided. Open for K: (1) the send rule: someone marks it ready, a reminder goes out the day before, and nothing is sent otherwise; (2) turn-taking, or everyone typing at once; (3) the 1st at 8:00 AM Central; (4) each issue readable on the site; (5) whether it replaces the weekly "News by email" or both run; (6) opens and clicks not tracked; (7) the name: "Louisiana Chess Bulletin" or "LCA Newsletter".
